author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Wolfeboro selectmen have rejected demolition of the Libby Museum and agreed to pursue a path that could place the historic building under new stewardship.

The vote followed two public hearings in August where residents strongly supported preserving the structure. Board members also agreed to seek a meeting with the New Hampshire Attorney General’s Charitable Trusts Unit and local preservation groups to map out the required legal process.

A newly formed Libby Museum Preservation Society wants to become the successor trustee through Carroll County Probate Court and use private funding to restore or rebuild the property while continuing its natural-history mission. The museum opened in 1912 and its building has been closed since 2024 because of mold, structural deterioration and deferred maintenance.

The decision keeps the building standing, but it does not by itself reopen the museum or settle who will manage it. Officials still must address the collection, restoration costs and court approvals. The board’s immediate action removes demolition as the preferred option and creates room for a preservation plan.
dek: The board voted to keep the historic natural-history museum standing and begin work toward new stewardship after strong public support for preservation.
headline: Wolfeboro selectmen reject demolition of Libby Museum
